questions.prompt: Which look should the Card stat preset carry: the CardStat Stat story as proposed, or Tile's current look?
questions.signsOff: the anatomy of the Card stat preset that replaces Tile: label position, label colour and plane

recommendation.rationale: The proposed preset is Metric anatomy on a filled Card one plane up: the figure first (heading face, text-primary), then an uppercase text-secondary label, 120 px wide in the story. Tile is the inverse: a 10 px bold text-tertiary label over a 14 px mono value on the raised plane. Tile's look is the denser one and it is what SessionMetrics and ScheduleTiles render today, which is why the PR keeps it pixel-for-pixel through the wrapper. The preset is the library's answer (roadmap decision 1: the stat is a Card preset composing Metric), reads at a glance from further away, and puts the label on text-secondary, which clears AA where Tile's text-tertiary label does not in dark. Pick the preset; Tile's consumers keep their look.

questions.signsOff: CardStat as the Card stat preset, Metric's labelPosition and valueStyle, and Tile rendered over CardStat

recommendation.rationale: Tile over CardStat is a zero-pixel refactor: this round rendered the Tile Row story from main's own Tile.tsx and from the head, dark and light, and both pairs measure 0 differing pixels (the implementer's 16 pairs agree). The preset itself is new (the Stat story): a filled Card at elevation 1 holding a Metric, with tone for the value colour. Metric gains labelPosition and valueStyle so Tile can keep its label-above, hex-tinted look through the wrapper; both are additive. The 684-line snapshot churn is FileActivityDetail's characterise snapshot picking up the wrapper's extra View. No token, no layout change outside the new story.

questions.signsOff: fenced code blocks (mono, language label, horizontal scroll) and pipe tables (ui/table, delimiter-row alignment) in MarkdownProse

recommendation.rationale: The CodeBlocks story shows a bash fence with its language label on text-secondary and the long command line clipped at the block's edge, where it scrolls sideways instead of wrapping, and an unterminated ts fence that runs to the end of the body. The Tables story shows a three-column pipe table on ui/table with the delimiter row driving alignment (Task left, Owner centre, Done right) and the ragged last row padded to the header. The Default story is unchanged: 0 differing pixels against main in both themes. One head-only defect, small but real: the rule under the language label is painted black in both themes (the gate reads #000000 on the dark plane, 1.34:1; in light it is the hard dark line under BASH and TS, darker than the block's own edge), because `border-b border-border-subtle` sits on the Text element and the colour class does not apply to it. A one-line move of the border onto a View fixes it. Ship with that as a follow-up, or ask for the fix round first if a black rule in light bothers you.
